record.notes: Published in July 2025 in Icelandic as 'Aðgerðaáætlun um gervigreind 2025-2027' (ISBN 978-9935-570-03-1) and in English (ISBN 978-9935-570-05-5); the government announced the English edition on 1 July 2025 and the Icelandic one on 2 July 2025. The plan is valid for two years from publication, with a review every six months and a comprehensive review no later than mid-2027; Iceland's 2021 AI strategy is to be reviewed in parallel. It builds on that strategy and on a November 2024 report on the economic opportunities of AI in Iceland, and each action names a responsible ministry, an implementing body and a time frame. The EFTA's EEA-Lex database lists the AI Act as under scrutiny for incorporation into the EEA Agreement by Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway (as stored on 17 October 2026).

verification.note: Recheck of 17 Oct 2026: re-read the Government of Iceland news item of 1 July 2025 and the English plan PDF from the government library (both stored 11 Oct 2026; the PDF as the record's secondary source). Stored in this run: the Icelandic news item of 2 July 2025 and the Icelandic plan PDF from the government library, which give the Icelandic title, July 2025, the publisher and a separate ISBN, and the EFTA's EEA-Lex entry for Regulation (EU) 2024/1689. The English edition carries the ministry's imprint and its own ISBN and does not call itself a translation, so it is recorded as one of the issuer's own texts. efta.int is not on the list of official sites, so the EEA-Lex quote counts as secondary. Version 1's notes on a November 2024 draft consultation, secondary sources describing a 2024-2026 plan with 25 measures and the absence of an AI bill in the Althingi rested on no stored file and were removed.

summary.quote: The government's first Action Plan on Artificial Intelligence sets out its main focuses and actions that support them.
Actions are categorised, based on their content and objectives, into five basic pillars that form the core structure of the plan.
The Action Plan also reflects Iceland's Strategy on Artificial Intelligence of 2021.
The EU has adopted harmonised legislation on AI for the internal market, which is currently being incorporated into the EEA Agreement.

The action includes assessing the need for adaptation arising from the transposition of the EU legislation and the associated costs, as well as preparing draft legislation introducing the necessary amendments to Icelandic law.
This includes defining which institutions have roles under the legislation
A bill on Artificial Intilligence. Objective Action Product Spring 2026.
Among other things, consideration will be given to information disorder, propaganda techniques and external interference in democratic decision-making processes.
with the aim of formulating general standards and guidelines for transparency and the responsible use of AI in political activities
Impact of AI on Democratic Debate and Decision-Making 5 July 2025 Iceland’s AI Action Plan 2025-2027 Autumn 2026.
Work will continue on developing and expanding a centralised set of standards and guidelines for public bodies at different levels of government to utilise AI safely and effectively.
including guidelines for the procurement of AI solutions. 16 Objective Action Product Spring 2027.

judgment.status_reasoning: A non-binding government action plan published on 1 July 2025 and valid for two years from publication, so until about July 2027. Nothing stored shows it was withdrawn or replaced; 'Published (non-binding, current)' stands on 17 October 2026.
judgment.scope_reasoning: A national AI action plan whose actions include preparing the AI Act implementing bill, analysing AI's effects on democracy and standards for safe public-sector use; in scope, as in version 1, with no note.
judgment.date_reasoning: The news item gives 1 July 2025; the PDF gives July 2025. The full date rests on the official news item.
